'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**[[Solhan and Tadaryat massacres]]
***At least 160 people are killed by [[Islamic extremism|Islamic extremists]] in Solhan, [[Yagha Province|Yagha]], northeastern [[Burkina Faso]]. It is the deadliest terrorist [[terrorism in Burkina Faso|attack]] in the [[history of Burkina Faso|country's history]]. Hours before the massacre, 13 civilians and a [[Burkina Faso Armed Forces|soldier]] were killed in an attack in [[Tadaryat]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-57368536 (BBC News)]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**Seventeen people are killed and five more injured during a rocket attack near a petrol station in the city of [[Marib]], [[Yemen]]. The incident is blamed on the [[Houthi movement|Houthis]], who however did not claim responsibility. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/6/houthi-missile-kills-at-least-17-in-yemens-marib-government (Al Jazeera English)]
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**Clashes erupt in [[Ayeyarwady Region|Ayeyarwady]] and [[Kyonpyaw]], near [[Yangon]], where the [[Tatmadaw|military]] shot and killed 20 protesters, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll since the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état|February 1 coup]] to more than 845. Meanwhile, [[military junta]] leader [[Min Aung Hlaing]] meets with [[ASEAN]] leaders to discuss paths to peace in the country. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/clashes-spread-myanmars-ayeyarwady-delta-several-killed-2021-06-05/ (Reuters)]
*[[Kurdish–Turkish conflict (2015–present)|Kurdish–Turkish conflict]]
**A [[Turkish Air Force|Turkish]] [[airstrike]] at the [[Makhmour Refugee Camp]] in northern [[Iraq]] kills three people and injures many others. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/turkish-air-strike-kills-least-three-refugee-camp-inside-iraq-2021-06-05/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*The [[Group of Seven]] [[finance minister]]s agree on a deal to commit towards a minimum global [[corporate tax]] rate of at least 15 percent, which will be aimed at preventing [[tax haven]]s that cater to large [[multinational corporation]]s, during a meeting in [[London]]. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1442105/g7-nations-reach-historic-deal-to-tax-big-multinationals (''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]
*[[President of El Salvador|Salvadoran President]] [[Nayib Bukele]] announces at a [[Bitcoin]] conference in [[Florida]] that his country will adopt the cryptocurrency as legal tender alongside the [[United States dollar|U.S. dollar]], making [[El Salvador]] the first country to do so. He plans to introduce the relevant legislation to the [[Legislative Assembly of El Salvador|Legislative Assembly]] next week. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-57373058 (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*A [[coal mine]] [[mining accident|collapse]] and subsequent flood leaves seven [[coal mining in Mexico|miners]] trapped in [[Muzquiz Municipality|Múzquiz]], [[Coahuila]], [[Mexico]]. [[Search and rescue|Rescue]] operations are currently underway. [https://news.sky.com/story/seven-miners-trapped-following-collapse-and-flooding-at-mexico-coal-pit-12325305 (Sky News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
****[[China]] becomes the first major country to authorize the emergency use of the [[Sinovac]] [[CoronaVac]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] for children as young as three years old. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-06-05/china-allows-preschoolers-to-get-emergency-covid-19-vaccine (Bloomberg News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]]
****[[Sri Lanka]] surpasses 200,000 cases of [[COVID-19]]. [http://www.adaderana.lk/news.php?nid=74423 (Ada Derana)] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan]]
****[[Taiwan]] reports a record 38 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 225. [https://amp.scmp.com/news/china/politics/article/3136180/taiwans-covid-19-deaths-break-single-day-record (''South China Morning Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium]]
***[[Belgium|Belgian]] [[Government of Belgium|federal]] and [[Communities, regions and language areas of Belgium#Regions|regional]] health ministers agree to open [[COVID-19 vaccination|vaccination]] for teenagers aged 16 to 17 years old using [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]]. The programme will begin once the vaccination of adults has been completed. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2021/jun/05/coronavirus-live-news-delhi-lockdown-india-cases-covid-uk (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela]]
***[[Venezuela]] reaches an agreement to buy doses of the [[Russia]]n [[EpiVacCorona]] [[vaccine]], as well as manufacture the vaccine locally. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-venezuela-russia/venezuela-to-purchase-and-manufacture-russias-epivaccorona-vaccine-idUSKCN2DH0D3 (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Anqing stabbing attack]]
**A man stabs random pedestrians on a street in [[Anqing]], [[China]], killing 6 people and wounding 14 others. The attacker is arrested and acted due to 'family problems'. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/police-china-apprehend-suspect-knife-attack-that-killed-6-injured-14-2021-06-06/ (Reuters)]
*[[Aftermath of the 2021 United States Capitol attack]]
**The [[United States Department of Justice|U.S. Department of Justice]] says that over 465 people have been arrested since the [[2021 United States Capitol attack|attack]] on the [[United States Capitol]]. The Department of Justice is also seeking information on 250 other suspects. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/150-days-capitol-attack-465-arrested-fbi-seeks/story?id=78103940 (ABC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]]
**[[2020–21 PGA Tour]]
***After completion of the third round of the [[Memorial Tournament]], [[Jon Rahm]] is notified that he had tested positive for COVID-19. Rahm was leading the tournament by 6 strokes before having to withdraw due to Tour protocols. [https://www.cbc.ca/sports/golf/jon-rahm-pga-golf-covid-19-memorial-1.6055073 (CBC News)]
